translations.text: Lo! We have heard heroes tell, men bold in deeds declare, what happened in the days of Maximian, who throughout the world, a wicked king,

…stirred up persecution, killed Christian men and threw down churches. The heathen war-leader poured out on the grassy plain the blood of those who praised God, the blood of the holy, of those who did what was right.
His kingdom was broad, wide and glorious over the nations of men, reaching over almost all the vast earth.
Mighty thanes went through the cities, as he had commanded. Often they stirred up violence, led astray in their deeds, those who hated the Lord's law through wicked craft.
They stirred up hostility, set up heathen idols, killed the holy, broke the learned, burned the chosen, and tormented God's warriors with spear and flame.

There was a certain man, rich in possessions and of noble family, a powerful reeve. He ruled fortified cities and guarded his homeland. He lived most of the time in the city of Nicomedia and kept a treasure-hoard there.
Often, against the word of God, he sought out heathen idols and shrines, very frequently and eagerly. His name was Heliseus; he held great and famous authority.
Then his heart began to love a maiden, Juliana (desire overcame him). She held holy faith in her spirit, and she was firmly resolved to keep her virginity pure of every sin for the love of Christ.
Then the maiden was betrothed to the wealthy man by her father's will. He did not fully know how things would turn out, or how she, young in spirit, scorned that union.
The fear of God was greater in her mind than all the treasure that lay among that nobleman's possessions.
Then the rich man, the man wealthy in gold, was eager in mind for the marriage, that the maiden should be made ready for him as quickly as possible, a bride for his home.
She firmly rejected that man's love, even though he owned riches under the lock of his hoard and countless ornaments on earth.
She scorned all of it, and spoke these words in front of the crowd of men: "I can tell you that you need not trouble yourself any further.
If you love and believe in the true God, raise up his praise, and acknowledge the protector of souls, I will be ready at once, without wavering, to do your will.
But I also tell you this: if by your deeds you commit yourself to a lesser god through devil-worship and call on a heathen idol, you cannot have me, and you cannot force me to be your wife.
You will never prepare pain so severe, through the violent hatred of harsh torments, that you could turn me away from these words."

When the nobleman, stained with wicked deeds, heard the maiden's words, he became swollen with anger. Fierce and blind of mind, he ordered swift messengers to fetch the holy maiden's father quickly for counsel.
Voices rose up after they leaned their spears together, those warriors. Both of them were heathen and sick with sins, the father-in-law and the son-in-law.
Then the guardian of the realm, the spear-bearer, spoke with a fierce heart to the maiden's father: "Your daughter has shown me dishonour.
She tells me outright that she cares nothing for my love as a kinsman or for my friendship. In my heart those insults are the greatest pain: that she rebuked me so angrily in front of this people,
and ordered me to worship a foreign god with riches, above the others we knew before, to praise him in words and honour him in my mind, or else not have her."
Then the father-in-law, the maiden's father, strong of mind, grew dark at these words and opened his heart: "I swear this by the true gods, as I hope ever to find favour with them, or

to find your grace, prince, in the wine-halls of the cities: if these words you tell me are true, dearest of men, I will not spare her. Instead, famous prince, I will hand her over to destruction, into your power.
Condemn her to death if that seems fitting to you, or let her live, whichever you prefer."
Then he went boldly to speak with the maiden, resolute and angrily perverse, swollen with rage, to where he knew the young woman, glad of heart, kept her dwelling.
Then he spoke these words: "You are my daughter, the dearest and sweetest in my heart, my only one on earth, the light of my eyes, Juliana!
In your folly, through your defiance, you have taken up a useless course, against the judgement of the wise.
You reject your bridegroom too strongly, of your own will. He is better than you, nobler on earth, richer in treasures of wealth. He is good to have as a friend.
So it is right that you do not reject the love of this man, a lasting and happy love."
Then the blessed Juliana gave him an answer (she had firmly established her friendship with God):

"I will never agree to be joined in kinship with this prince unless he worships the God of hosts more eagerly than he has so far, and loves with offerings the one who created light, heaven and earth and the expanse of the seas, and the whole circle of the world's dwellings.
Then in anger the father gave her a hostile answer; not at all did he [?] adornments:
Then the blessed one, wise and dear to God, Juliana, gave him answer: "I will tell you the truth; as long as I live I will not tell a lie.
but I honour the Lord of glory, of the world and of majesty, and I trust in him alone for everything, that he may be my protector, helper and saviour against the fiends of hell."

Then before the people the ruler of the people, fierce in mind, spoke threatening words and grew very angry. Out of malicious vengeance he ordered the sinless maiden to be stretched out naked and beaten with whips.

Let the strife rest, this hateful quarrel among the people. If after this you go on following error through your foolish will, then I shall of necessity, driven by hostility, avenge in the grimmest way the offence against the gods,
the angry slander that you have begun to utter with blasphemies against the best and the mildest of those that men know, whom this people has long worshipped among them."
The noble spirit answered him unafraid: "I do not fear your judgments, accursed criminal, nor the evil of your torments.
I have as my hope the Guardian of the heavenly kingdom, the gentle protector, the Ruler of hosts, who will shield me against your sorcery, from the grip of the hostile ones whom you count as gods.
They are lacking in every good: empty, useless, unprofitable. No man will find any benefit there, or true peace, though he seeks friendship from them.
Then the prison door, the work of hammers, was shut with a lock. The holy one, steadfast in faith, remained inside.
The Holy Spirit was her constant companion. Then suddenly there came into that prison-house the enemy of men, skilled in evil.

He had the form of an angel, the enemy of souls, skilled in causing grief, the captive of hell. He spoke to the holy woman: "What are you suffering, you who are the dearest and most honoured to the King of glory, our Lord?
This judge has prepared the worst torments for you, endless pain, if you will not offer sacrifice, wise-minded one, and please his gods.
Be quick, when he orders you to be led out from here, to offer sacrifice promptly, a victory offering, before death takes you, death in front of the company of men.
In that way, blessed maiden, you shall escape the judge's anger."
Then she, who was not afraid and who was pleasing to Christ, boldly asked where he had come from.
The outcast answered her: "I am an angel of God, come down from above, an excellent thegn, and I have been sent to you, holy, from on high.
Hard and wondrously cruel torments have been prepared for you as a deadly punishment. God, the Son of the Ruler, has commanded that you be told to protect [?] yourself from them."
Then the maiden was struck with terror at the sudden message that the monster, the adversary of glory, spoke to her.
Then the young woman, without guile, began to steady her mind firmly and to call on God: "Now I will ask you, protector of men, eternal Almighty, by the noble creation which you,
Father of angels, established in the beginning, that you not let me turn away from praising your blessed gift, as this messenger who stands before me announces to me a perilous, sudden message.
So I will ask you, merciful one, glory of kings, guardian of majesty, to make known to me what this thegn is, flying through the air, who urges me away from you onto a hard road."

A beautiful voice answered her from the clouds, uttering words: "Seize that insolent one and hold him fast until he tells his errand truthfully, all of it from the beginning, and what his origins are."
Then the maiden's spirit was gladdened, she who was glorious in her judgment. She seized that devil [?] "to deliver the King of all kings to death.
Further, I contrived that the soldier began to wound the Ruler, in the sight of the multitude, so that blood and water both together poured down to the earth.
Again, I put it into Herod's mind to order John beheaded, when the holy man rebuked him with words for his love of the woman, an unlawful marriage.
I also taught Simon, with cunning thoughts, to start a quarrel with the chosen thegns of Christ, and to attack the holy men with scorn through deep heresy, saying they were sorcerers.

I ventured with crafty tricks when I deceived Nero, so that he ordered Christ's thegns, Peter and Paul, to be killed. Before that, Pilate hanged the Ruler of the heavens, the mighty Lord, on the cross at my instigation.
Likewise I also taught Aegeas, so that in his folly he ordered holy Andrew to be hanged on a high tree, so that he sent forth his spirit from the gallows into the splendour of glory.
Thus I, with my brothers, have committed many cruel evils, dark sins, which I cannot tell or recount in full, nor know the number of those harsh, hostile thoughts."
The holy Juliana answered him through the gift of the Spirit: "You must go further still, enemy of mankind, in telling your errand, and say who sent you to me."

The monster, seized with fear and with no hope of peace, gave her an answer: "Listen: my father, king of hell's inhabitants, sent me here to you on this journey from that narrow home. In that house of grief he is more eager for every evil than I am.
When he sends us to turn the mind of the righteous through deception and to turn them away from salvation, we are sad of mind and afraid in spirit.
Our lord, that terrible prince, is not gentle with us if we have done no evil; after that we dare not go anywhere into his presence.

Then he sends thegns out of the darkness throughout the wide earth and orders them to stir up violence: if we are met on the earth's paths, or found far or near, they are to bind us and scourge us with torments in the surging fire.
If, despite hindrance, the mind of the righteous, the thought of the holy, does not turn away, we suffer the hardest and worst torments through painful blows.
Now you can see the truth in your own mind: I was forced by necessity into this venture, oppressed time and again, so that I came to you."
Then again the holy woman began to question in words the enemy of men, the worker of strife, the originator of ancient sins:
not just a few times, with wounds of sins, so that you yourself may know more clearly that this is true, not false.
With bold thought I believed and was sure that I could turn you away from salvation easily, by my skill alone,
he will not betray God, but, bold in prayer, he holds his ground firmly on foot. Then I must turn away far from there, humiliated, robbed of joys, into the grip of the flames, to lament my grief,

the tower is pierced and the entrance opened when I first send bitter thoughts into him, into his heart, through a flight of arrows, through the various desires of the mind, so that it seems better to him to commit sins, the lusts of the body, than to praise God.
"I thought that you would have to be all the warier of such an encounter with the righteous, and all the less bold, since he has often withstood you, through the King of glory, against your will."
you have placed your trust in the eternal God, who sits in majesty, the Lord of mankind, just as I fix my hope on my father, the king of the dwellers in hell.

When I am sent against the righteous to turn their minds to wicked deeds and their hearts away from salvation, sometimes my will and my hope are denied among the holy, because they resist me, just as sorrow befell me here on my journey.
The devil answered her: "Now I hear from your words that I must, of necessity and forced by afflictions, reveal my mind as you command me, and endure harsh compulsion.
Some whom I found without the sign of God, careless and unblessed, I boldly killed with my own hands through various deaths, by cunning devices.
Then the reeve, a man with a gallows-minded heart, ordered Juliana, holy in spirit, to be led out of the narrow building to his judgment seat to speak with the heathens.

Then an angel of God came, shining in splendour, and thrust the fire aside. He freed and protected her, pure of guilt and without sin, and scattered the fiercely greedy flame. The holy one, the chief of maidens, stood unharmed in the middle.
The fiend was not slow. He taught him to order an earthen vessel to be made with wondrous skill, amid the din of war, and to surround it with tree-trunks and wood.

Neither her fringe nor her garment, nor her hair nor her skin, nor her body nor her limbs were marked by the fire. She stood in the flame wholly unharmed and gave thanks for everything to the Lord of lords.

Then the judge grew fierce and savage-minded and began to tear his garment. He also bared his teeth and gnashed them, raged in his mind like a wild beast, roared in his gallows-minded rage, and blamed his gods because their might could not withstand the woman's will.

Then suddenly the abject spirit of hell came, wretched and miserable, singing a song of harm. He was the accursed one whom she had earlier bound and beaten with torments. Full of sorrowful songs, he cried out before the crowd:
"Now it is very likely that she will humiliate wretched me again with evil miseries, as she did to me before."

My soul must leave the body on a journey to an unknown dwelling, and I myself do not know where. I must go from here to seek another place in keeping with my former works, to go according to my deeds of old.

Sorrowful, C (ᚳ), Y (ᚣ) and N (ᚾ) will depart. The King, the giver of victories, will be stern when E (ᛖ), W (ᚹ) and U (ᚢ), stained with sins, wait in terror for what he will judge for them according to their deeds, as the reward for their lives.

I ask every man of the human race who recites this poem to remember me by my name, for I am in need, and to pray earnestly to the Lord that the protector of the heavens, the ruler of powers, give me help on that great day,

the Father, the Spirit of comfort, in that perilous hour, the judge of deeds, and the beloved Son, when the Trinity, sitting in majesty in unity, assigns to every member of the human race a reward according to his works throughout the bright creation.
